title: k-th Smallest in a Sorted Matrix

concept.title: Binary search on the value, count with the staircase
body: The `n` by `n` matrix is sorted in every row and every column, but not as a whole. To find the k-th smallest value, binary search on the **value** `v` between the smallest cell (top left) and the largest (bottom right). For a candidate `v`, count the cells that are `<= v`. The k-th smallest is the smallest `v` for which this count is at least `k`.

The count uses the staircase walk from the previous problems: when you move to the next row, the boundary `j` can only move left, so the whole count costs O(n). The binary search needs about 31 rounds for 32-bit values.

statement: An `n` by `n` matrix has rows sorted left to right and columns sorted top to bottom (in non-decreasing order). Find the k-th smallest number among all its `n * n` cells, counting duplicates separately (the 1st smallest is the smallest cell).
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `n` integers each.
hints: Binary search on the value between the top left and the bottom right cell.
Count the cells not larger than the value with a staircase walk in O(n).
If the count is at least k, the answer is at most the value, otherwise it is bigger.
